title: Hyperparameter Tuning — Choose the Oven Before Baking
key_insight: Hyperparameters are choices made before training, such as tree depth. Parameters are values the model learns from data, such as split locations.
body:
## Choose the Oven Before Baking

A baker chooses temperature before a loaf goes in, then the loaf’s inside changes while baking. Those are two different kinds of values.

Hyperparameters are choices made before training, such as tree depth. Parameters are values the model learns from data, such as split locations.

Try choices on validation data, not the final test. The sealed test judges the complete recipe after the choice is made.
common_mistakes: Tuning on the final test set.
Reporting only the winning trial and hiding instability around it.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Choose the Oven Before Baking” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Good settings can matter as much as the chosen algorithm, but careless search overfits validation data.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Choose the Oven Before Baking” story, explain Hyperparameter Tuning without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
